original_value: Soil moisture is a key component of the water cycle budget. Sensing soil moisture using microwave sensors onboard satellites is an effective way to retrieve surface soil moisture (SSM) at a global scale, but the retrieval accuracy in some regions is inadequate due to the complicated factors influencing the general retrieval process. On the other hand, monitoring soil moisture directly through in-situ devices is capable of providing high-accuracy SSM measurements, but the distribution of such stations is sparse. Recently, the Global Navigation Satellite System interferometric Reflectometry (GNSS-R) method was used to derive field-scale SSM, which can serve as a supplement to contemporary sparse in-situ soil moisture networks. On this basis, it is of great research significance to explore the fusion of these different kinds of SSM data, so as to improve the present satellite SSM products with regard to their data accuracy. In this paper, a multi-source point-surface fusion method based on the generalized regression neural network (GRNN) model is applied to fuse the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) Level 3 radiometer SSM daily product with in-situ measured and GNSS-R estimated SSM data from five soil moisture networks in the western continental U.S. The results show that the GRNN model obtains a fairly good performance, with a cross-validation R value of approximately 0.9 and a ubRMSE of 0.044 cm3 cm−3. Furthermore, the fused SSM product agrees well with the site-specific SSM data in terms of time and space, which demonstrates that the proposed GRNN model is able to construct the non-linear relationship between the point- and surface-scale SSM.

result.paraphrase: Soil moisture is a vital part of the water-cycle budget. Microwave satellite sensors can retrieve global surface soil moisture (SSM) effectively, but accuracy is poor in some regions because the overall retrieval process is influenced by complex factors. Direct monitoring with in-situ instruments can provide highly accurate SSM measurements, yet station coverage is sparse. More recently, the Global Navigation Satellite System interferometric Reflectometry (GNSS-R) approach has been used to estimate field-scale SSM, offering a supplement to today’s sparse in-situ soil-moisture networks. Based on this, it is important to investigate fusing these different SSM data types to improve the accuracy of current satellite SSM products. In this paper, a multi-source point-surface fusion method using a generalized regression neural network (GRNN) model is applied to combine the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) Level 3 radiometer SSM daily product with in-situ measured and GNSS-R estimated SSM data from five soil moisture networks in the western continental U.S. The results indicate that the GRNN model performs well, with a cross-validation R value of about 0.9 and a ubRMSE of 0.044 cm3 cm−3. In addition, the fused SSM product matches the site-specific SSM data well in both time and space, showing that the proposed GRNN model can capture the non-linear relationship between point-scale and surface-scale SSM.
